content.user_title: Coauthor Clear Documents with Structured Review
content.value_statement: Important documents often fail because context, structure, and reader assumptions remain unclear. This skill guides collaborative drafting, focused revision, and reader testing through a repeatable three-stage workflow.
actual_capabilities: Collects document goals, audience details, templates, constraints, and supporting context through targeted questions.
Proposes a tailored document structure and creates a Markdown scaffold with section placeholders.
Brainstorms 5 to 20 candidate points for each section before the user selects priorities.
Drafts and refines sections through focused edits based on explicit user feedback.
Reviews completed documents for coherence, redundancy, contradictions, ambiguity, and unsupported assumptions.
Tests reader comprehension with sub-agents or provides a manual fresh-conversation testing process.
limitations: Requires accurate context and timely feedback from the user.
Cannot access shared documents or team channels without configured integrations and appropriate permissions.
Requires manual reader testing when sub-agents are unavailable.
Does not replace fact-checking, technical validation, legal review, or final owner approval.

use_cases.title: Draft a Product Requirements Document
use_cases.description: Build a product requirements document that aligns goals, constraints, stakeholders, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Develop a Technical RFC
use_cases.description: Develop an RFC or technical specification with explicit trade-offs, dependencies, risks, and unresolved questions.

use_cases.title: Record a Team Decision
use_cases.description: Create a decision record or proposal that explains context, alternatives, rationale, and expected impact.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me coauthor a [document type] for [audience]. The desired outcome is [outcome]. Start by asking me the essential context questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a document when only the purpose and audience are known.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a draft of [document]. Review its structure and ask questions about missing context. Then help me revise one section at a time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Strengthen a draft without replacing the entire document.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Template and Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this template: [template]. Gather context from the materials I provide and propose a section order. Identify the section with greatest uncertainty. For each section, brainstorm options before drafting. Apply only the changes I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a structured document from a template and several source materials.

prompt_templates.title: Run Advanced Reader Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Coauthor an executive decision document from [context]. Track unresolved assumptions and stakeholder concerns during drafting. After revision, test the document with a fresh sub-agent. Report comprehension gaps, repair affected sections, and repeat testing until the stated exit criteria pass.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce and validate a high-impact document for executive readers.

output_examples.input: Create a decision document for adopting a managed event queue.
output_examples.output: Decision: Adopt a managed event queue. Context explains current delivery failures. Options compare cost, ownership, and reliability. The recommendation records risks, mitigations, and success measures.

output_examples.input: Help structure an RFC for replacing session storage.
output_examples.output: The RFC covers goals, current constraints, proposed architecture, migration steps, failure handling, observability, security considerations, alternatives, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Test whether new engineers can understand this deployment guide.
output_examples.output: Reader testing finds unclear prerequisites and an undefined rollback condition. The revised guide adds access requirements, verification steps, rollback ownership, and expected recovery time.

best_practices: Provide the audience, desired outcome, constraints, and source materials before drafting begins.
Give specific feedback about what to keep, remove, combine, or clarify after each section.
Verify facts, links, permissions, and technical claims before approving the final document.
anti_patterns: Do not request a polished final document before sharing essential context.
Do not grant integrations broader access than the document task requires.
Do not treat fresh-reader feedback as a substitute for domain expert review.

faq.question: Which document types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports technical specifications, RFCs, product requirements, proposals, decision records, and other substantial business documents.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing document?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the draft and goals, then the skill reviews structure and applies focused revisions with your approval.

faq.question: Can it read shared documents or team channels?
faq.answer: Yes, when compatible integrations are configured and you provide appropriate access. Otherwise, paste or upload the relevant material.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: A fresh AI instance answers realistic reader questions using only the document. This exposes ambiguity, missing context, and hidden assumptions.

faq.question: Can I skip part of the workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. You can skip stages, shorten brainstorming, or switch to freeform writing when the full process is unnecessary.

faq.question: Does the skill verify every factual claim?
faq.answer: No. The document owner must verify facts, links, technical details, and conclusions with authoritative sources or qualified reviewers.
